key_components.Canvas3DSaddle: Three.js / React Three Fiber interactive 3D hyperbolic paraboloid z = K*(x^2 - y^2) surface with Raycasting for vertex dragging
key_components.Canvas2DPoincare: Alternative 2D Poincaré Disk Projection canvas showing curved arcs intersecting boundary at 90 degrees
key_components.AngleSumCard: Hero HUD card displaying dynamic Angle Sum (alpha + beta + gamma), Angular Defect delta = 180° - Sum, and Area relation
key_components.CurvatureControl: Precision slider with snap points (0 Euclidean, -0.5 Moderate, -1.0 Deep Hyperbolic) with visual curvature response
key_components.VertexTelemetry: Coordinates & angle breakdowns for Vertex A (Cyan), Vertex B (Emerald), Vertex C (Magenta) with real-time degree updates
key_components.ExplanationDrawer: Collapsible interactive guide explaining Gaussian curvature K, geodesic triangles, parallel postulate violation, and Gauss-Bonnet theorem (Area = -K * Defect)

motion_and_effects.canvas_effects: Subtle particle stars/grid in background, bloom/glow effect on geodesic lines using Three.js shader or CSS drop-shadow filters
motion_and_effects.vertex_pulse: Continuous glowing ring animation around active draggable vertices
motion_and_effects.defect_alert: Color transition on Angle Sum text from emerald (180°) to bright amber (<180°) as negative curvature increases
motion_and_effects.transitions: Smooth camera interpolation when toggling between 2D Poincaré view and 3D Saddle view

instructions_to_main_agent: Build a state-of-the-art interactive mathematical visualization for hyperbolic geometry using Three.js (or Canvas2D/WebGL) in React.
Ensure 3D saddle geometry is generated mathematically using z = K * (x^2 - y^2) or hyperbolic metric geodesics.
Implement draggable vertices A, B, and C with full mouse/touch drag controls. Constrain drag to surface or 2D disk appropriately.
Calculate geodesic curves between A-B, B-C, C-A along the hyperbolic surface and render them as neon glowing tubes or multi-segment paths.
Compute tangent vectors at each vertex to calculate internal angles alpha, beta, gamma accurately.
Display floating overlay degree labels next to A, B, C directly over the 3D canvas using CSS transform / screen projection coordinate math.
Provide a prominent 'Live Angle Sum Display' (e.g. '132.4° < 180°') highlighting the defect delta = 180° - sum.

Provide a Curvature Slider (K from 0.0 to -2.0). When K=0, the triangle behaves strictly as a Euclidean triangle with sum = 180°. As K becomes negative, geodesics curve inward/outward and angle sum drops below 180°.
Include 2D (Poincaré Disk) vs 3D (Saddle Surface) view toggle mode.
Include a 'Reset Vertices' button to return A, B, C and Curvature to default preset states.
Include a short, elegant, interactive explanation panel breaking down: Euclidean vs Hyperbolic, Gauss-Bonnet Theorem (Area = Defect / |K|), and Why straight lines curve in negative space.

All buttons, sliders, vertex tags, toggle switches, and metrics MUST include clear data-testid attributes (e.g., data-testid='curvature-slider', data-testid='angle-sum-display', data-testid='toggle-2d-3d').
Ensure dark IDE/observatory styling using Tailwind CSS with glassmorphism backdrop blurs (`backdrop-blur-md bg-slate-900/80 border border-sky-500/20`).
Use Sonner for toasts when vertex resetting or preset actions occur.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Do NOT use generic Inter font for main headings. Use technical monospace/sans pairing (JetBrains Mono, Outfit, Fira Code).
Maintain APCA compliant contrast ratios for mathematical data text.
Ensure exact data-testid attributes on all interactive controls (buttons, inputs, sliders, toggles) for automated test suites.
Ensure mobile responsiveness with auto-collapsible HUD panels on narrow screens.
No transparent backgrounds on dropdowns, modals, or header overlays without backdrop-blur filters.
